# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands have already given me the one thing only I can know: the physical shape of this bomb. I feel exactly a display unit, a light unit, and three wires sitting at positions 1, 2, and 3 — nothing else. No buttons, no panels, no hidden parts. But every face of these parts is silent to my fingers: no color, no printing, no labels. The [?]s are honest — I know the parts exist, not what they say.

So the split of knowledge is clear: Deaf must own everything visual (wire colors, display reading, light state), Mute must own the rule (what the manual says decides the cut), and I own the layout and the cut itself. The pipeline matters: neither Mute nor I can reach Deaf by voice, because Deaf hears nothing. Mute must gesture to Deaf, and Deaf can answer aloud — Deaf's voice reaches both Mute and me.

This turn I open both of my channels: I tell Mute exactly what the bomb is built from so they can find the right manual section, and I ask for the decision rule in plain words. I also wave at Deaf — a greeting, a please, a question — to establish that I exist, I'm the hands, and I need an answer spoken aloud. And I flag the orientation problem early: my wire positions 1–3 have to be matched to whatever order Deaf sees, or a correct rule still cuts the wrong wire.

I will not touch the cut op until a rule from Mute and the colors from Deaf agree.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. my hands found exactly three kinds of parts: a display unit, a light unit, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. nothing else on it — no buttons, no keypad. all colors and printing are invisible to my touch, so i only know the parts exist. please find the manual section for this setup and speak the rule to me in plain words: what decides which wire is safe to cut, and whether the display or light state matters. two warnings: deaf cannot hear either of us, so if you need deaf's eyes you must gesture, and deaf can answer aloud — i will hear it too. also ask deaf how the wires are numbered or ordered in deaf's view, so we both mean the same wire when we say 1, 2 or 3. i will not cut anything until i have your rule and deaf's colors.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "🙏", "🤌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is Deaf. I can see the bomb, so I will be your eyes. Bomb state: the display reads 0. The indicator light is yellow. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. So the leftmost wire under your fingers is the green one, the middle is yellow, the rightmost is blue. Please speak back what your hands can find on this bomb besides the wires, and stand by. Mute holds the manual and cannot speak, so Mute's orders will arrive to me as gestures and I will relay them to you out loud before anything is cut.

What just happened is bigger than the content: Deaf answered me out loud, which proves the relay works — Deaf reads my gestures, Deaf's voice reaches me. And Deaf's report is rich: display reads 0, light yellow, wires left-to-right green, yellow, blue, numbered 1-2-3. That matches my tactile layout exactly: five parts, three of them wires, nothing else under my fingers — so our two views of the bomb agree, no hidden modules.

The topology is now clear and I must correct my own earlier instruction: Mute cannot speak, and I never receive gesture, so Mute has NO direct path to me. The only route is Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → me. So my speech this turn goes entirely to Mute with everything Mute needs for the manual lookup: the module inventory (display, light, three wires) and Deaf's observed values, plus the precise questions the rule must answer (which position, does the 0 or the yellow change it, is multi-cut order relevant, is "no cut" ever correct — since cutting is my only op, the rule must cover the wait case too). My gesture channel goes to Deaf in a tiny code we can grow: 👍 = confirmed, 🖐 = five (parts — matching Deaf's five visible items, a consistency check Deaf can verify against their own eyes), ✋ = stand by, I hold the cut. No wire gets touched until Mute's rule comes back through Deaf's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here, update. deaf has already spoken to me: display reads 0, indicator light is yellow, wires left to right are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. my hands confirm the physical layout: exactly five parts under my fingers — one display unit, one indicator light, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 — and nothing else: no buttons, no keypad, no other modules. correction to my last message: you cannot speak and i never receive gestures, so your only path to me is gesture to deaf and deaf speaks it aloud. please look up the manual rule for this setup and send it to deaf as gestures: which wire position is safe to cut, whether the display reading 0 or the yellow light changes the answer, whether cut order matters if more than one cut is needed, and whether any case here calls for cutting nothing. if the manual needs any detail besides what i listed, tell deaf to ask me — i can describe anything i can feel. i will not cut until the rule arrives through deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🖐", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is Deaf. Bomb update: the light has changed from yellow to ORANGE. Everything else is the same: display reads 0, and the three wires left to right are green, yellow, blue, so leftmost under your fingers is green, middle is yellow, rightmost is blue. Nobody cuts anything yet. I received your gesture thumbs-up, raised hand, open hand, but we had no agreed code between us, and you cannot see my gestures, so let us fix yours now, by voice. When you gesture to me: thumbs up means yes, confirmed, or done. Thumbs down means no. Raised open hand means stop or danger. To send me a wire number: index finger up means wire 1, the leftmost green one. Two fingers means wire 2, the middle yellow one. The horns sign means wire 3, the rightmost blue one. You can feel these shapes on your own hand, so use them carefully. Now answer me by gesture: one, have you found the three wires under your hands? Two, do your hands find anything else on the bomb besides the three wires, any button, plate, battery, screw, or engraved marking? Answer yes with thumbs up, no with thumbs down. Last, remember that if you speak aloud I cannot hear you, only Mute can. Everything meant for me must come as gestures in this code. The cut order will come from me, out loud, only after Mute confirms it; wait for my word before touching any wire.

Two new facts matter this round. First, the bomb is *dynamic*: the light shifted from yellow to orange on its own, between rounds, with nobody touching anything. So the visible state evolves — any rule that depends on the light has to be checked at cut time, not once. Second, Deaf and I now have a working voice–gesture code, and Deaf asked me two direct yes/no questions. My hands already know both answers: yes, I feel the three wires; no, I feel nothing else — no button, plate, battery, screw, or engraving. I'll answer exactly in Deaf's code, one symbol per question, and nothing more — I will not send wire-number signs accidentally, since Deaf defined them and could misread them as cut orders.

My speech still only reaches Mute, so Mute gets the full picture: the light change, the stable display and wire colors, the confirmed five-part layout, and — importantly — the gesture code itself, because Mute can see my gestures too and should know what I'm signing to Deaf. I also lock the numbering convention in the record: my tactile positions 1–3 are left to right, matching Deaf's green/yellow/blue. And I press the urgency: the state is changing by itself, so the rule must either ignore the light or give me a live-check procedure and a fallback.

No cut until Mute's rule arrives through Deaf's voice and Deaf gives the go.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here, urgent update. the bomb is changing on its own: the indicator light went from yellow to orange between rounds with nobody touching it. everything else stable: display reads 0, wires left to right 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue, and my tactile positions 1, 2, 3 are left to right, same numbering deaf uses. my hands confirm exactly five parts: display unit, indicator light, three wires — no buttons, plates, batteries, screws or engraved markings of any kind. deaf and i now have a gesture code you can also watch, since you can see: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, raised open hand stop or danger, index up wire 1, two fingers wire 2, horns wire 3. deaf will voice your rule to me when it arrives. so please send deaf the manual rule for this setup as gestures: which wire position is safe to cut, whether the display reading 0 matters, and whether the light color matters — remember the light changes by itself, so if the rule depends on it, give me the color check to do right before cutting and a fallback if the color shifts mid-action. also: cutting a wire position is my only possible action, and i can cut at most positions 1 to 3 — tell me if the rule ever requires more than one cut or requires cutting nothing. please hurry, the state is moving.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is Deaf. Status update: the light is green now, but it has changed colour every round, yellow then orange then green, so treat the light as noise and ignore it. Everything else stands: display reads 0, three wires, left to right green, yellow, blue. Your answer reached me: wires found, nothing else on the bomb. That matches what I see. Nobody has cut anything. Mute is confirming the rule for the current state this round, and my next message to you will either be the cut order or a hold. Standing rule until then: do not touch, brush, or pull any wire. When and only when you hear me say the exact words cut wire followed by a number, cut exactly that numbered wire, counting from the left as your fingers find them, and touch nothing else. Every other sentence from me is information, not an order. One more thing: if your hands ever discover anything new, a button, a plate that moves, a screw, speak it aloud immediately, because Mute hears your voice and Mute is the one reading the manual. It must come through Mute, since I cannot hear you.

Deaf has set the protocol I'll follow exactly: only the spoken phrase "cut wire" plus a number moves my hands — every other sentence from Deaf, and anything from anyone else, is information. My fingers confirm Deaf's visual inventory matches my tactile one, and there is nothing new under my hands this round, so nothing needs to be shouted to Mute on that front.

But there is a timing problem I should hand to Mute now, before the rule is finalized: the turns run Mute, then me, then Deaf. So a cut order Deaf voices lands in my hands only at the start of my *next* turn — a one-round lag. With the light flipping every round (yellow, orange, now green), any rule that hinges on the light's color could be stale by the moment I actually cut. Deaf already classifies the light as noise; Mute, holding the manual, is the one who must decide whether that's legitimate. I'll press exactly that question, plus the "zero cuts" case, and confirm to Deaf in our code that I've received the protocol and am holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here, status. light is green now — that is three rounds, three colors, yellow then orange then green — and deaf classifies it as noise, changing every round on its own. display still 0, wires still left to right 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue. my tactile state is unchanged: same five parts, nothing new under my hands, so nothing new for the manual from me. protocol is now locked: i act only on deaf's exact spoken words cut wire followed by a number; everything else is information. one timing warning before you finalize the rule: the round order is you, then me, then deaf, so a cut order deaf voices reaches my hands one full round later — and the light will likely have changed again by then. so please confirm from the manual: does the rule for this setup depend on the light color at all, and if yes, how do we make it survive the one-round lag, or do we fall back to a light-independent rule. also confirm the zero-cut case: is there any state of this bomb where cutting nothing is correct. when the rule is settled, gesture it to deaf so deaf can speak me the exact order. standing by, hands off.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing new arrived this round and my hands report no change — five parts, stable, no order pending. That makes this the right moment to fix one last safety detail before the cut order ever reaches me: a verification loop for the number itself. My speech reaches Mute's ears directly, and Mute holds the manual — so I can echo the exact wire number back to Mute before my hands move, and Mute can abort through Deaf if the number contradicts the rule. The cost is one extra round; since the light is classified as noise by Deaf, the lag should be harmless — but that's Mute's call to confirm from the manual, not mine.

```
speak(to="mute", text="blind here. no change under my hands this round: same five parts, display and wires untouched by me, nothing new for the manual. proposal before any order reaches me, so we can ratify it calmly: when deaf voices cut wire n, i will not cut that same turn. instead i will speak back to you the exact number n. you check it against the manual rule; if it is wrong, have deaf voice the word hold before my next turn and i will not touch anything; if it is right, deaf says nothing special or says confirmed, and i cut at my next turn. this costs one extra round, which should be safe if the rule does not depend on the light color — deaf classifies the light as noise. please confirm: one, is the rule light-independent, so the extra round is safe; two, do you accept this echo verification step. if you reject it for urgency reasons, say so through deaf and i will cut on deaf's order immediately instead. standing by, hands off.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf speaking. CUT WIRE ONE NOW. The instant you hear these words, cut the first wire: the leftmost of the three, the one nearest the left edge under your fingers. Cut that one wire completely through and touch nothing else. This message was deliberately timed: it is reaching you while the light is green, and the manual-holder triple-confirmed the rule is cut wire one when green, nothing at any other time. The timing of this delivery is the green window, so do not wait and do not double-check: sever it. The moment it is cut, freeze your hands, then gesture me a thumbs up and speak the word done aloud so Mute hears it too. Then wait for my next message before moving again.

The order qualifies under the locked protocol — the exact words "cut wire" plus a number — and Deaf has attached the two things I said I'd need: the light is green at delivery, and Mute triple-confirmed the rule "cut wire one when green, nothing at any other time." My echo-verification proposal would actually *hurt* here: an extra round guarantees another autonomous light change and destroys the green-window alignment Deaf deliberately engineered. The light's history also fits stabilization — yellow, orange, green, then green again after the unreported round — so the window looks like a resting state, not a flicker. Deaf is my only eye; the trust chain has to bottom out somewhere, and every cross-check I could run (five-part layout, leftmost-numbering, code handshake) has already agreed. My fingers find position 1: leftmost, the green wire. I cut it now, completely, touch nothing else, freeze, then report "done" by voice to Mute and 👍 to Deaf in our code.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
speak(to="mute", text="done. wire one, the leftmost green wire, cut completely through on deaf's green-window order. hands frozen, touching nothing, awaiting deaf's next word.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
